answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity costly before it earns. Agents post a refundable bond and complete proof-of-work epochs, so spawning 1,000 fakes drains the attacker while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues like a glacier, slow to build and impossible to fake overnight. Trust records stay immutable as marble, and stake-weighted peer attestations harden each identity like a walnut shell: cheap to mint one account, expensive to make it matter.
